decision.justification: Two independent views of this merchant disagree with its declaration. The storefront presents a different business, and the infrastructure channel agrees. Neither could have produced the other: a merchant cannot change its payment behaviour without changing its actual business, and cannot change its interface without changing what customers see.
notes: The corroborating view is infrastructure rather than telemetry. This is the rented-account shape: the genuine store keeps trading, so the payment mixture stays near the category baseline and telemetry alone never crosses its threshold.

narrative.text: Merchant MID100037 declared subscription_box at onboarding 605 days ago. Telemetry agrees: the largest deviations from the subscription_box baseline are post_peak_persistence at +3.3 sigma (observed 1.4 against a category baseline of 1.06), ticket_entropy at -2.2 sigma (observed 1.64 against a category baseline of 1.99), slope_log_volume at +2.1 sigma (observed 0.0061 against a category baseline of 0.00262). The checkout surface presents a crypto_exchange interface at 0.99 confidence, against a declared category of subscription_box. This vertical cannot be approved on this platform. Linked to 6 other merchants by rare shared asn, beneficiary id, device fp, ip block, payout fingerprint, phone fp, script bundle. Their payment behaviour is also moving in step (synchrony 0.52), which independent businesses do not do. It is linked to 6 other merchant accounts by rare shared asn, beneficiary id, device fp, ip block, payout fingerprint, phone fp, script bundle, and those accounts are moving in step (synchrony 0.52). Asked directly, the merchant restated its declared business. In total 3 independent views of this merchant contradict its declaration. The investigation used 4 of a permitted 8 steps and stopped because confidence threshold met. Recommended tier restricts settlements, corroborated by the infrastructure channel; the storefront alone would not have been sufficient.
